findings.highlight: That was always Kiritsugu's favorite saying.
findings.evidenceJa: それが切嗣の口癖だった。
findings.governingReading: The wish that no one be sad and that one's limited help make the surrounding world livable was Kiritsugu's frequent stock phrase.
findings.explanation: Kiritsugu's habitual phrase becomes his favorite saying.

findings.highlight: But Kiritsugu wanted to do something for those he couldn't see or reach.
findings.evidenceJa: だが、切嗣は目に見えない部分までなんとかしたかったのかもしれない。
findings.governingReading: Shirou thinks Kiritsugu may have wanted to do something even for the parts of the world beyond his sight.
findings.explanation: Shirou's conjecture about Kiritsugu's wider aim becomes fact.

findings.highlight: If in the process of trying to save a thousand, you overlook five hundred...
findings.evidenceJa: 千を得ようとして五百をこぼすのなら。
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu contrasts trying for a thousand and losing or letting five hundred slip away with deliberately abandoning one hundred to keep nine hundred alive.
findings.explanation: Losing five hundred while trying to save a thousand becomes overlooking them.

findings.highlight: But I still believed that a hero of justice could save everyone, despite those limitations.
findings.evidenceJa: けど、それでも—それを踏まえた上でみんなを助けるのが正義の味方なんだって信じていた。
findings.governingReading: A hero tries to realize the ideal even if it is an unattainable fantasy.
findings.explanation: The definition of a hero changes from attempting an unattainable ideal to being capable of performing miracles.

findings.highlight: Results are the most important thing. But apart from that, what's even more important is to have the heart—
findings.evidenceJa: 結果は一番大事だ。けどそれとは別に、そうであろうとする心が—
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu says results are most important, then begins to add that separately there is the heart that tries to be so; the remembered sentence cuts off before its predicate.
findings.explanation: Kiritsugu's unfinished contrast is completed into a hierarchy that contradicts his first clause.

findings.highlight: "Of course. Even from my point of view, Shirou is really composed. So much so, he might be overdoing it."
findings.evidenceJa: 「当然です。士郎はわたしでもちょっと趣味に走りすぎたかっていうぐらい落ち着いてるんだから」
findings.governingReading: Taiga says Shirou is so composed that even she wonders whether she has indulged her own tastes too much; the boast implies influence over how he has turned out.
findings.explanation: The English keeps the joke about excessive composure but removes Taiga's reference to indulging her own tastes. Her implied credit for Shirou's temperament becomes criticism of his excess.

findings.highlight: "Oh, don't worry. I'm going to make sure I tell her every single word you just said. I'm sure if I tell her about how happy Emiya was when he heard about her predicament, why, I bet she'll break ten stacks of tiles from sheer delight!"
findings.evidenceJa: 「今の話、一言一句間違えずに伝えてあげるから安心して。衛宮くんも喜んでたって言ったら、綾子ったらそりゃあもう瓦十枚はぶち抜くぐらいに喜ぶんじゃないかな」
findings.governingReading: Rin sarcastically imagines Ayako being delighted enough to smash through ten tiles.
findings.explanation: Ten tiles become ten stacks of tiles, enlarging Rin's comic threat. The sarcastic delight and playful pressure on Shirou remain.

findings.highlight: "...I...would like to amend my statement. See, it was just a figure of speech. It's not something I'd be proud if people heard, so I would really appreciate if you kept it to yourself."
findings.evidenceJa: 「—訂正したい。今のは言葉のあやだ。あまり人様に話すような発言じゃないんで、黙っていてくれると、とても助かる」
findings.governingReading: Shirou says the remark is not something he wants repeated to other people and politely asks Rin to stay silent.
findings.explanation: Shirou's formal retraction contains a malformed proud construction.

findings.highlight: "Oh I'm sorry. Don't get me wrong. I'm not playing around here."
findings.evidenceJa: 「あら、ごめんなさい。別に楽しい訳じゃないから誤解しないでね？」
findings.governingReading: Rin tells Shirou not to misunderstand: she is not enjoying this; he knows with certainty that she is.
findings.explanation: Rin denying enjoyment becomes denying that she is joking.

findings.highlight: "Got it. I'll start making Western-style breakfasts from now on.
findings.evidenceJa: 「……分かった。これから朝食は洋風にする。
findings.governingReading: Shirou offers Western breakfasts as the price of silence and says he may even feel willing to accept Rin's earlier proposal that breakfast should use bread.
findings.explanation: Shirou's conditional concession becomes mere repetition of Rin's request.

findings.highlight: Fine then, I'll serve bread for tomorrow, so no more complaints, right? So what was said here, stays here. Don't you dare blab about this to Mitsuzuri."
findings.evidenceJa: お望みどおり明日から朝はパンにするから、それで文句はないな？　ならさっきの話は他言無用、絶対に美綴にはバラすなよ」
findings.governingReading: Shirou says breakfast will be bread beginning tomorrow.
findings.explanation: Starting tomorrow becomes serving bread for tomorrow.

findings.highlight: Fuji-nee shakes her head disapprovingly as she eats.
findings.evidenceJa: こまったもんだ、と頷いてごはんを食べる藤ねえ。
findings.governingReading: Calling the situation troublesome, Taiga nods and keeps eating after cheerfully announcing she will tell Ayako.
findings.explanation: Taiga's self-satisfied nod becomes a disapproving head shake.

findings.highlight: "Yeah, but let me off the hook just for today, Fuji-nee. It's not that I don't like school. There's something I have to do, and it's just more important right now. So let me go."
findings.evidenceJa: 「嘘だけど、それで勘弁してくれ藤ねえ。何も学校がイヤって訳じゃないんだ。やる事があって、そっちのが今は重要なだけなんだ。だからさ、それで許してくれないか」
findings.governingReading: Shirou admits the injury is a lie, explains that something else matters more now, and asks Taiga to excuse or permit his absence.
findings.explanation: Shirou asking permission to miss school becomes asking to be allowed to leave.
